definitions.explanation: Dried stalks of rice or other grain plants left after threshing. Traditionally used as a material for ropes, mats, sandals, thatched roofs, and natto wrappers, and as bedding for livestock.

examples.japanese: {屋根|やね}がわら⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{葺|ふ}かれて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The roof is thatched with straw.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧わら⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{草履|ぞうり}→草履：04048_zouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}っていた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: People long ago made sandals out of straw.

examples.japanese: ⟦{溺|おぼ}れる→溺れる：02026_oboreru⟧⟦{者|もの}→者：12734_mono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧わら⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧つかむ、⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{望|のぞ}み→望み：03543_nozomi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すがった。
examples.english: As the saying 'a drowning person clutches at straws' goes, he clung to one last hope.

notes:
Also written with the kanji {藁|わら}, though the hiragana form is more common in everyday writing. Refers chiefly to rice straw in Japan, given the centrality of rice cultivation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- わら{細工|ざいく}: straw craft
- わら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{屋根|やね}→屋根：02264_yane⟧: thatched roof
- わら⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すがる: to clutch at straws (idiomatic — to grasp at any hope)
- わら{半紙|ばんし}: cheap straw-pulp paper (used in schools)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional straw products like ⟦{草鞋|わらじ}→草鞋：29127_waraji⟧ (straw sandals), ⟦{注連縄|しめなわ}→注連縄：06015_shimenawa⟧ (sacred Shinto ropes), and straw-wrapped ⟦{納豆|なっとう}→納豆：04930_nattou⟧ are still seen today, especially at shrines and in regional foods.
